title: The gerund: two actions at the same time

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the gerund *corriendo* in *Llegó corriendo* and *Volvimos a casa cantando* for actions at the same time from B1 Unit 2, and *estar* + gerund from A1 Unit 19. The gerund says what the subject of the main verb is doing while the main action happens. It does not change for person, tense, gender or number.

items.spanish: Los guerrilleros pasaban meses en las montañas, planeando ataques.
items.english: The guerrilla fighters spent months in the mountains, planning attacks.

items.spanish: Los oficiales estudiaban en la escuela, aprendiendo técnicas militares.
items.english: The officers studied at the school, learning military techniques.

items.spanish: Algunos grupos respondieron con violencia, radicalizándose cada vez más.
items.english: Some groups answered with violence, becoming more and more radical.

items.spanish: Otros buscaron el cambio participando en elecciones y en sindicatos.
items.english: Others sought change by taking part in elections and in unions.

sections.content: The gerund always shares its subject with the main verb: in *Los oficiales estudiaban aprendiendo técnicas*, the officers both studied and learned. If the two actions have different subjects, use *mientras* or *cuando* instead.
